subject: Optimize Toolkit: packaging, discount sweep & technical clarifications
messages:

Thanks Dylan — quick follow ups after our call:

1) On discounts: can you confirm what a 12-month committed band at 1.2B tokens/year looks like in terms of effective unit price assuming we adopt the recommended caching + batching profile you suggested?
2) On quantization: our ML team is concerned about hallucination risk at 4-bit on the summarization model. Any middle ground?
3) Can we get a one-page takeaway that lists the packaging options and what triggers a recharge/retro credit if we outdrive the pilot?

Attachment: edgemap_requirements_v3.pdf

—Ethan

Head of Infrastructure, Edgemap

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: initial pricing questions on Optimize toolkit

Ethan — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and I'll loop Monica for the technical nuance: 

- Commit band pricing: for 1.2B tokens/yr the commercial delta vs on-demand is significant. With the caching/batching baseline we presented on the call (per-route TTL of 30s, prefix-KV for common prompts, continuous batching target at 40–60ms latency window) the effective per-1k-token price falls ~28% vs standard hosted. I will send the detailed sheet.

- Quantization: Monica will weigh in; short answer is we recommend an "adaptive" quant profile (int8 for generation-heavy paths, 4-bit for read-heavy embedding routes). We can scope a pilot to validate hallucination risk on a narrow prompt set.

- Pilot vs production mechanics: we do have retroactive credit mechanics for overage in the first 90 days of a committed roll if you exceed pilot projections by <20% and then sign a 12-month commit within 30 days. I'll attach the one-pager.

Looping Monica for a quick bulletized technical note.

—Dylan
Principal Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Wells <ethan.wells@edgemap.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: technical note — quantization and caching recommendations for Edgemap

Ethan — hi, Monica from Solutions Engineering. A few practical notes after reviewing the requirements PDF: 

Summary recommendations (short):
- Hybrid-quant profile: use int8 for generative flows (summarization, long-form completion) and 4-bit for high-volume embedding/semantic search paths. This gives a good cost/quality balance and limits hallucination exposure.
- Per-route TTLs and per-customer KV namespace: configure conservative TTLs (30–120s) for workstreams where prefix reuse is predictable; use a separate KV namespace for high-consistency routes to avoid cross-tenant cache churn.
- Batching & latency SLOs: continuous batching with a 40ms collection window yields 2–3x token cost savings on bursty queries while keeping median p50 latency under 200ms for 2k context models.
- Safety/QA: include a narrow reverification prompt set (20–30 examples) for the summarizer to validate quality at int8; if quality delta > 5% on your eval metrics we'll recommend stepping up to int16 for that variant.

Operational things to note:
- Pilot credits & retro policy: as Dylan mentioned, we offer a 90-day overage buffer; technical overrun analysis is required to qualify.
- Fallback policy: set an automatic fallback route to an unquantized variant for time-sensitive endpoints (configurable per-route).
- Rollout plan: we suggest canarying quantization on 10% of traffic for 2 weeks and monitor perplexity + hallucination ops.

I'll attach a short configuration checklist and a conservative loss-of-quality estimate table. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with your ML team next week.

Attachments: optimize_toolkit_config_checklist.txt (text), quant_quality_delta_example.csv

—Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Wells <ethan.wells@edgemap.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-13T13:50:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial proposal: commit bands, sweep discount and credit mechanics

Ethan — following up with a commercial offer aligned to the technical path Monica proposed. Key points: 

Offer structure (condensed):
- 12-month commit: 1.2B tokens/year at a headline 30% discount vs list (reflects batching/caching baseline).
- "Swept" efficiency credit: if your observed efficiency (tokens consumed per normalized unit of user activity) exceeds our joint projection by >15% for two consecutive months, we will issue a one-time efficiency credit equal to 8% of the monthly invoice applied to the subsequent month (this is our "sweep discount" mechanic).
- Pilot conversion overage: as Dylan said, first 90 days we allow up to 20% over the signed pilot projection with a provisional retro-credit if you convert to a 12-month commit within 30 days of pilot end.
- Early pay incentive: 2% invoice credit on annual prepay.

Contract/Procurement asks:
- We can hold headline pricing for 30 days. Need an NDA + PO to proceed to SOW and SOC2 evidence handover.

I've attached a clean pricing worksheet and a draft terms summary. If the sweep-credit language looks good we can bake that into Exhibit B to avoid delays.

Attachments: optimize_toolkit_pricing_sheet.xlsx, exhibit_b_sweep_credit_draft.docx

—Karthik
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Wells <ethan.wells@edgemap.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-14T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: contract mechanics and next steps (NDA / PO)

Ethan — quick note from legal to keep momentum moving: 

- We can accept the sweep-credit mechanic as defined; will require a simple metric appendix to Exhibit B that defines the "efficiency" metric (we recommend tokens-per-active-session measured at the API route level).
- For the pilot retro-credit we need a 30-day window from pilot end to execute the conversion; please confirm you have internal PO timing.
- SOC2 evidence and procurement checklist: we'll publish an evidence bundle once NDA is in place (link provided in the Drive folder).

If Edgemap can share a PO or sign the attached one-page ordering document, we'll hold pricing through 2028-06-13 and target a technical kickoff the week after SOW execution.

Thanks — looping Karthik for commercial follow-up and Monica for the technical kickoff.

—Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
